# Scoped dependency audit following the reported ledger-implementation dispute

Audit date: 3 November 2026. This is a local source-and-dependency inspection, not a new experiment, a new assessment of the intended framework, or a reconstruction of another session's timing or billing. No tests were run for this audit. Historical files remain unchanged.

## Finding

**The named disputed runs have not been identified in the searched local material. The current package does inherit the preceding review as a runnable archive, and that review contains standard-model calculations described in places as repairs or a replacement thesis. Those descriptions need an explicit framework-fidelity qualification.** Mathematical correctness of a specified covariance, Saha, Hermite, or finite-moment model does not establish that it implements the author's Direction–Spin–Throughput and connection-energy construction. Nor does a failure or limitation of one of those restricted models reject that construction.

The supplied alert is treated as a user-reported dispute about another implementation. This audit neither confirms its reported times nor attributes the disputed runs to the current project. It also does not establish that the relevant original package was read by another assistant. No exact package-to-code mapping for that framework is present in the reviewed mathematical notes. Framework fidelity therefore remains **unverified**, rather than verified, falsified, or disproved by the present controls.

## Search scope and name collisions

The first bounded search covered 222 text/code files in the current formal tree and 21 in the preceding review, excluding generated artifacts, duplicated relocated/package-test trees, runtime/toolchain directories, raw HTML, and the original source directory. The source follow-up covered 593 text/code/JSON files under the preceding `sources/` and 182 under current `incoming_disk/` (the latter overlaps the first search). Parsed string values in `incoming_disk/metadata/drive_text_payloads.json` were searched separately without printing their payloads. Searches used word boundaries and the labels `E9`, `Heegner`, `midrange`, `split-at-zero`, `rally`, `Direction–Spin`, `Throughput`, `04:25`, `05:45`; related `connection energy`, `two books`, `two ledger`, `single clock`, `population`, `commutator`, and repair language was inspected selectively. This is a local search statement, not a claim that the named work does not exist elsewhere.

## Places requiring interpretation changes

The strongest issue is not a demonstrated wrong matrix identity. It is possible overextension from a standard surrogate to the author's intended framework.

| Exact location | Existing claim or framing | Required treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Preceding `reviews/matter_audit.md:14,107–120` | “useful repair,” “Strongest repair preserving the work,” “Replace,” and “Suggested replacement thesis.” | Preserve as historical proposed standard-model continuation. Withdraw any implication that this replaces or corrects the complete Direction–Spin–Throughput/connection-energy framework. No source-faithful mapping has been demonstrated here. |
| Preceding `reviews/matter_audit.md:32–34,130` | Gas-at-rest normality and entropy-production qualifications; an eight-mode Hermite/BGK example. | The operator-dependent mathematical cautions stand. Explicitly limit the counterexample to the declared operator and norm; it does not decide the author's intended ledger variables or connection-energy observable. |
| Preceding `build_review.py:128–131,166` | General-sounding conclusions adjacent to the Hermite result. | Add that the example answers only a literal unrestricted normality claim for standard kinetic generators. It is not a tested realization or rejection of the intended framework. |
| Preceding `reviews/votkp_gas_bridge.md:130–139`, especially `:138` | Historical failure list and “no scalar-only … clock … bound”; a zero commutator for a closed Hermitian atomic Hamiltonian. | Preserve as reports about the named restricted records/models. The zero commutator is correct for that Hamiltonian, but does not identify the user's connection energy with that commutator. No inference against a richer direction/spin/throughput record is justified without deriving the mapping. |
| Preceding `build_review.py:52,116` | Existing sources “contain … needed repair”; block identities “repair the proposed extension.” | Qualify this as the proposed positive-covariance continuation under declared assumptions, not a repair of every part of the author's programme. |
| Current `manuscript/front.md:5,9,23,44` | Distinct objects, standard models, evidence classes, and chapter plan are already explicit. | Add the compact dependency notice below, so readers do not infer that conditional formalization certifies framework fidelity. |
| Current `review/formal_review.md` | Analytical approval of B/K/D/G/R/M/P statements. | Append that approval is of displayed hypotheses and proofs, not a certification that the user's intended ledger model has been implemented. This addendum can be referenced rather than rewriting every theorem. |

The relevant original Matter source itself identifies the dynamic paragraph as an analogy: preceding `sources/Matter_v5_release/matter_at_a_scale_v5.tex:538–540`. The ensuing normality prose is at `:540–555`, with throughput and entropy production at `:575–581`. That matters: the review can flag missing hypotheses in literal broad claims without pretending that a surrogate calculation falsifies the intended construction. The original hypothesis/analogy marking must travel with any quotation or summary.

## Current bounded models that can remain, with their proper status

- Current `math/boundary_theorems.md:3` already identifies standard finite-dimensional mathematics and distinguishes analytic proof from Lean verification. Its positive-covariance statements remain conditional theorems; they neither encode nor refute all ledger variables.
- Current `gas/formal_gas_response.md:3,47,187,207,349` explicitly bounds the finite Saha model, its temperature response, scale covariances, and implementation checks. `gas/gas_peel_inverse.md:49,77` correctly distinguishes a synthetic inverse identity and an excited-partition control from measurement. These can remain as **standard equilibrium benchmarks**, without claiming that a population vector is the whole intended state.
- Current `math/moment_matched_transport.md:176` says exactly what its construction establishes: density–flow–stress alone fails to determine later force-free transport for arbitrary positive velocity distributions. Its separate erasure toy is not a reconstruction of the user's dynamics. The result concerns omitted higher moments, not an argument that direction/spin/throughput is ineffective.
- Current `manuscript/moment_records.md:31,41` restricts non-determination to the stated finite moment record and labels the finite-difference construction standard. These statements can remain; a richer record is outside their no-go hypothesis.
- Preceding `tests/thermal_census.py:42,69–83` states its synthetic scope and implements the explicit matrix `A=-Q-iM`, with `Q=diag(0,0,0,1,1,1,1,1)`. The calculation establishes nonnormal contraction in that fixed weighted finite model. Neither population bookkeeping nor its one collision-time scale establishes fidelity to a multiple-book construction.

## Recommended exact notice for current front matter and reproduction notes

> **Framework-fidelity limitation.** This edition proves and checks explicitly stated covariance, finite-moment, equilibrium-population, and reduced-response models. It does not yet establish that these implement the complete Direction–Spin–Throughput or connection-energy construction. The author has reported a separate implementation dispute involving E9 repairs, a Heegner helper, midrange and split-at-zeros checks, and rally/commutator tests; those named runs have not been identified in the local inputs inspected here. Preserved earlier review language describing a “repair” or “replacement” is historical and is not an endorsed replacement of that intended framework. Its surrogate-model results may not be used to reject that framework without a documented source-to-equation-to-code mapping. Reproducing a calculation or checking a conditional theorem does not supply that missing mapping.

A shorter theorem-review addendum is sufficient:

> The analytical approvals in this review concern the displayed hypotheses and derivations. They do not certify that a standard model is a source-faithful implementation of the author's full ledger framework. See `contamination_dependency_audit.md` for the disputed-implementation boundary and inherited-review qualifications.

## Decision

Keep the exact proofs, declared finite-model outputs, original inputs, and failed historical hypotheses. Mark the framework attribution as unresolved and the affected replacement language as historical/disputed. Do not publish the questioned interpretation as settled, do not silently delete provenance, and do not run another surrogate experiment as a substitute for reading and mapping the intended model. This audit makes no finding about another session's timing, billing, or culpability.
